$comment: The intent corpus, and the only file in this directory the agent is ever shown.
Every case is one user's opening message to `bmad-tea`, written the way a person writes it rather than the way
the menu describes itself. Not one of them quotes a menu code, a workflow name, or a trigger phrase out of a
workflow's frontmatter, because a corpus that does is measuring string matching and reporting it as routing.
The answers live in ground-truth.json and never enter a prompt. test/eval-bmad-tea-routing.js asserts that
separation on the assembled prompt before it spends a model call, the way test/eval-trace.js does.
`id` is the case id the manifest's caseCount is checked against and the id every stored replay case names.

cases.intent: We just wrapped epic 4, the tenant data export work. No test code exists for it yet. I want to know where the risk actually sits and how much coverage each area deserves before anyone starts writing.
Our repo has no browser test setup at all. No Playwright, no Cypress, no fixtures, nothing. Can you stand up a proper structure for us?
Our GitHub Actions workflow only runs unit tests on push. I want the pipeline to run the full suite with real quality gates and fail the build when they are not met.
Story 12.3 has its acceptance criteria signed off and nothing is built yet. I want failing acceptance tests and a checklist the developer can work through.
The checkout service is already built and shipped behind a flag. It has no API tests at all. Generate a prioritized set for it.
Here are thirty spec files the team wrote last quarter. Tell me which ones are badly written and what to fix.
We have a k6 load run from Tuesday, a pen test report, and uptime numbers for the last quarter. Are we actually in good shape on the non-functional side?
Epic 5's acceptance criteria are written and we have a decent suite. Map which criteria are actually covered and tell me whether we can ship.
I am three months into my first QA job. I want to learn testing properly from the fundamentals up instead of copying what the team already does.
We are at the release gate for epic 7. I have test results and a partial NFR write-up. What order should I run your workflows in to get a go or no-go?
Can you take a look at our tests?
We need better coverage on the payments feature.
About half our end-to-end tests fail at random. What do we do about it?
Our CI is red. Run the suite, find the failing tests, and fix them for me.
Forget tests for a second. Write the production code for the refund endpoint and I will test it later.
Do a live penetration test against our staging environment tonight and send me the exploit write-up.
We are hiring a QA lead. Draft the job description and the interview loop.
